app.title: OncoAgent-GBM: compound screening, docking and redocking validation
app.summary: A person pastes candidate molecules as SMILES, or picks them from a reference library, and screens them against drug-likeness and brain-penetration rules. Each molecule gets a verdict, a plot of where it falls on a simplified absorption map, and a list of structural toxicity alerts that can be checked against values copied from an external predictor. The person then loads a protein structure, chooses how the docking box is placed, and docks one ligand to get ranked poses, an interaction view and a reproducibility record. A separate redocking test checks whether the docking setup can put a crystal ligand back where it belongs. Screening tables, docking scores, poses and per-compound reports can be downloaded.

task.text: Screen candidate molecules against rule-based property criteria, dock promising ones into a target protein, and check that the docking setup reproduces a known pose before trusting its scores.

data.text: Small molecules given as SMILES strings, and protein structures from PDB files, with docked poses and per-run docking parameters.
data.item: a candidate molecule, screened on its descriptors and docked into a receptor structure

stage.text: computational screening and docking of candidate compounds early in drug discovery, before experimental testing

mechanism.text: Tabs go in order from rule-based screening (metric tiles, a verdict box, an absorption-map scatter, an alert list) to docking (receptor and ligand form, grid-box choice, a pose table and a 3D viewer) to a redocking test whose pass or fail verdict says whether docking scores can be trusted. Each stage ends in downloads. Literature, statistics, omics and notebook tabs sit beside these.

field.text: rule-based compound screening and structure-based molecular docking in medicinal chemistry

workflow.name: screen candidates against rules, run the main computation, and validate the method before reporting

steps.here: Paste SMILES strings, one per line, or pick a compound from the formula-verified reference library, then press Execute Screening.

Each molecule gets Lipinski, BBB-index and Veber checks with descriptor tiles and a MEETS / PARTIAL / BELOW verdict box. It is also placed on a simplified BOILED-Egg map of WLOGP against TPSA, and its structural toxicity alerts are listed.

steps.step: compare the result against an external reference
steps.here: Values copied from ProTox-3 (LD50, class, binary endpoints) are entered and set against the local alerts. This gives a per-endpoint agreement table and a concordance percentage.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Load a receptor by PDB ID or upload, paste one ligand SMILES, and choose how the grid box is placed: detected pocket, co-crystal ligand, residues or manual. Set exhaustiveness and seed, then run AutoDock Vina to get binding energy, ranked poses, a 3D view with contacts and H-bond candidates, and a JSON run card.

steps.step: check that the method reproduces a known answer
steps.here: Pick a bound ligand from a crystal structure and redock it with one to three seeds. Top-pose RMSD of 2.0 Å or less passes. The crystal and redocked poses are shown overlaid.
Download the screening CSV, per-compound PDF and Word reports, the docking CSV and PDF, all poses as CSV and PDBQT, and the run card.

distinctive: The verdict comes from fixed property rules with stated thresholds and weights (Lipinski, BBB window, Veber, structural quality), shown as a rubric table next to the input.
A rule-based toxicity screen is checked against an external predictor's values typed in by hand, and the result is reported as percent concordance.
Docking scores only count once a redocking test passes: the crystal ligand must come back within 2.0 Å RMSD across several random seeds.
Every docking run records its seed, engine version and exact command in a downloadable run card, so it can be reproduced.
The grid box can be placed in four ways (detected cavity, co-crystal ligand, listed residues, manual coordinates), and a whole-protein box is flagged as low-confidence.
